entry.title: A Place Plan for Palnackie 2025–35 Now Available

link.title: A Place Plan for Palnackie 2025–35 Now Available

entry.content:
A Place Plan for Palnackie 2025–35 is now available to read and download from the new Documents & Resources section of this website.

The plan is presented by Buittle Parish Community Council and was produced in association with Buittle Quest, the parish’s development trust. It was funded and supported by the Dumfries & Galloway Community Led Local Development Fund and Dumfries & Galloway Council.

Download the plan: A Place Plan for Palnackie 2025–35 (PDF, 6.1MB)

What is a Local Place Plan?

Local Place Plans are produced by communities and set out how they would like buildings, land and development in their area to be used. Dumfries & Galloway Council has encouraged communities across the region to produce them, and they feed into the Council’s next Local Development Plan (LDP3), which is due in 2027.

The plan isn’t a binding order. It gives the community a clear, shared statement of what matters here, which can support new projects and funding bids, and it can be updated as circumstances change. It builds on Finding New Ways for Palnackie, the community action plan published by the Community Council in 2018.

Built on what you told us

In July and August 2025, 275 questionnaires were hand-delivered to households in Palnackie and across Buittle Parish, with an online version also available. These responses, together with conversations with local businesses and voluntary groups and earlier consultations, shaped the plan.

The plan looks closely at six resources that have long been at the heart of village life: the Primary School, the Glenisle Inn, the Village Shop, Flounders Café, the Village Hall and the Port.

The plan’s priorities

  • Palnackie Primary School: find new uses for the school building that keep it serving the community, and address community asset transfer.
  • The Playpark: repair or redesign it (and possibly relocate it in time) to make the village friendlier for young people.
  • The Glenisle Inn: recognise and support the pub as a central part of community life.
  • The Village Shop, Flounders Café and accommodation: support the community-owned three-part project.
  • The Village Hall: widen the range of classes and uses, and plan improvements to the building.
  • The Port: manage it safely as a community resource. Funding permitting, that means repairing the north wall, limiting berthing to small boats, landscaping the north shore for public use, adding a heritage cabin and building a pontoon for small boats.
  • Housing: keep the community informed on upcoming private housing developments.
  • The Environment: map footpaths, trails and back roads, and encourage environmental growth and awareness.

The plan also covers community action, volunteering, resilience and the role of the Community Council and Buittle Quest. It’s well worth a read for anyone interested in Palnackie’s future.

Questions about the plan?

✉ community-council@palnackie.com
entry.summary: The Local Place Plan for Palnackie, setting out the community's priorities for the village's buildings, land and development over the next ten years, is now available to read and download.

entry.title: Palnackie Park Pals Receive Match Funding from Dumfries and Galloway Council

link.title: Palnackie Park Pals Receive Match Funding from Dumfries and Galloway Council

entry.content:
Great news for the Palnackie Children’s Park project: Dumfries and Galloway Council have announced that they will match fund whatever the Park Pals raise.

That means the £9,000 committed by TP Niven has effectively become £18,000, and the £1,000+ already raised within Palnackie is now worth £2,000+. And that’s before the group has even approached external funders, which is the next stage of work now underway.

The Park Pals group is raising funds to replace the village’s ageing children’s park with something safe, accessible, and welcoming for all ages — including toddlers and children with disabilities. Every pound raised locally now goes twice as far.

entry.summary: Dumfries and Galloway Council have announced they will match fund what the Park Pals raise for the new children's park — doubling the impact of every pound raised locally.

entry.title: Buittle Quest Embarks on North Shore Development Project

link.title: Buittle Quest Embarks on North Shore Development Project

entry.content:
As of June 2026, Buittle Quest is embarking on their biggest project to date. This is a dynamic time for the Port, with Scottish Water works now complete on the South Shore.

With funding support from Dumfries & Galloway Council’s Coastal Benefit Fund and Foundation Scotland, Buittle Quest are beginning the journey of making the North Shore of Palnackie Port both safe and accessible to the community. In the long term the charity hopes to develop an attractive destination for smaller leisure boats.

Events will be held locally to keep the community up to date and to give them the opportunity to feed in to developments on the North Shore. There will also be a heritage project to capture memories of Palnackie, giving the opportunity to promote the industrial and social heritage of the Port.

Keep an eye on the charity’s socials for updates.
